package_info.package_versions: All vulnerable MikroTik RouterOS versions (especially those affected by CVE-2018-14847)
package_info.why_malicious: The campaign compromises MikroTik routers by exploiting weak/default credentials and a known vulnerability (CVE-2018-14847), then deploys malicious SSH commands to reroute network traffic, establishing persistent C2 channels and evading detection.

execution_context.trigger: post-compromise (after gaining access via credentials or exploit)
execution_context.file_location: SSH shell session on MikroTik RouterOS

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ip firewall nat add chain=dstnat protocol=tcp dst-port=80 action=dst-nat to-addresses=<C2_IP> to-ports=<C2_PORT>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful compromise, the attacker issues a command to add a NAT rule that redirects incoming TCP traffic on port 80 to a remote C2 server, enabling persistent C2 communication and traffic redirection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Adding NAT rules to redirect traffic to external, attacker-controlled IPs is a classic sign of router compromise and C2 channel establishment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal router administration does not involve redirecting all HTTP traffic to unknown external servers without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network administrators may use NAT rules for legitimate port forwarding, but not to untrusted or unknown external IPs.
key_indicators: NAT rules redirecting to external, non-corporate IPs
Commands issued via SSH after unauthorized access

execution_context.file_location: RouterOS configuration (via Winbox, SSH, or API)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit CVE-2018-14847 to extract router credentials and configuration files
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At initial access, the attacker exploits CVE-2018-14847 to read sensitive files and credentials from the router, enabling further compromise and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exploiting a known vulnerability to extract credentials is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate users do not exploit vulnerabilities to access configuration files.
key_indicators: Unauthorized access to sensitive configuration files

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to MikroTik router via default credentials, brute force, or CVE-2018-14847 exploit.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute commands on the router

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues SSH shell commands to add NAT rules redirecting traffic to C2 infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes persistent C2 channel and traffic redirection

behavioral_signatures: Addition of NAT rules redirecting traffic to external IPs
Unusual SSH or Winbox access from unknown sources
Configuration file access via CVE-2018-14847 exploit patterns
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in /ip firewall nat configuration
Access logs showing use of Winbox or SSH from non-administrative IPs
network_indicators: Outbound connections from router to known Trickbot C2 IPs
Redirection of HTTP/HTTPS traffic to non-standard external addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor MikroTik router configurations for unauthorized NAT rules, especially those redirecting traffic to external or untrusted IPs. Audit access logs for signs of brute force, default credential use, or exploitation of CVE-2018-14847. Monitor for outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure and unexpected changes in router configuration files.
